\begin{example} \end{example}[Gaussian curvature in distance coordinates]

Source: petersen:page-0118, petersen:page-0119 ↗ lem:pet-ch3-jacobi-field-sectional-curvature-formula

1. ch3:3.2.12If $\dim M=2$, write $g=dr^2+\rho ^2(r,\theta )d\theta ^2$ with $\theta $ coordinatizing the level sets of $r$. Then $\partial _\theta $ is a Jacobi field of length $\rho $, and $\sec (T_pM)=-\partial _r^2\rho /\rho $. \end{example}
Proof

↗ ex:pet-ch3-two-dim-sectional-curvature-formula

\sketch By subsection 2.4, $J=\partial _\theta $ is a Jacobi field. The equations in subsection 2.4 give $\operatorname {Hess}r(J,J)=\rho \partial _r\rho $ and $S(J)=(\partial _r\rho /\rho )J$. Hence

\[ -\sec (J,\partial _r)\rho ^2 =\partial _r(\rho \partial _r\rho )-(\partial _r\rho )^2 =\rho \partial _r^2\rho , \]

where subsection 2.4 supplies the left-hand side. This yields the claimed formula.

□
